body:
WHAT
The engine's Read tool sends image files with certain extensions (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp) to a vision model. The app's file-attach picker offers the same extension list when vision is on. Because the app cannot import the engine, the list exists twice and must match.

WHY
A drift means the picker offers a file Read will refuse, or hides one it would accept.

WHERE
engine/tools/src/read.ts — `const IMAGE_TYPES` (extension → media type), used in `readTool.execute` via `IMAGE_TYPES[extname(path).toLowerCase()]`; app/main.js — `const IMAGE_TYPES` (around line 608) and the `context:pickFiles` IPC handler that derives `imageExts` from `Object.keys(IMAGE_TYPES)` for the dialog `filters`.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. The sorted key set of engine IMAGE_TYPES equals the sorted key set of app IMAGE_TYPES ({.png,.jpg,.jpeg,.gif,.webp}).
2. For every shared key, the media type string is identical on both sides (e.g. '.jpg' → 'image/jpeg').
3. With vision ready, the pickFiles 'Images' filter extensions equal the engine keys with the leading dot removed; with vision not ready the Images filter is absent and imageExts is empty.
4. Read of a file with an extension in the set and no vision model returns an isError result saying the image cannot be seen (not binary-file text), proving the engine treats exactly those extensions as images.
